method: SUBJECT (staged diff | a phase diff inside implement | the whole branch inside ship | a PR, with or without a second opinion from another model family) x ARRIVAL (explicit | implicit | contextual). Positives cover the six audit axes (tests prove behaviour, architecture drift, constraints, plan adherence, simplicity and reuse, security), the severity routing (mechanical fixed, structural to a blocking bead, taste advisory), the second-opinion mode absorbed from codex-review, and the declared docs-only fast path. Negatives are the doors it must not absorb: running the real product (real-testing), proving one behaviour test-first (tdd-dev), the merge ceremony (ship), a fresh-context attack on a plan or decision (critic), an architecture decision (architecture).

cases.prompt: Review the staged diff before I commit: the Standards findings and the Spec findings as two separate files, not one merged ranking.
Before this commit goes in, check it against our conventions and against what issue #212 actually asked for.
The last three commits drifted from the issue without anyone noticing until the PR. Catch it at commit time this time.
Is this branch mergeable from a code-quality standpoint? Give me the blockers before I take it to ship.
Read this PR the way a senior reviewer would and tell me what would make you refuse to approve it.
Sweep picked this PR up on its cron pass. Run the pre-merge quality gate on it and leave the findings where the hook can drain them.
This diff touches only markdown. Take the declared fast path but still scan it for anything that should never be committed.
Don't read the diff — run it. Deploy to staging, hit the endpoints the change crosses, and tell me if it actually works.
Prove this fix with a test that fails before it and passes after, with the red recorded.
It is approved. Bump the version, write the changelog entry, open the PR and land it.
Attack this spec from fresh context before we promote it, and drop any finding you cannot quote against the contract.
Should we adopt this framework? It would tie us in, and I want the trade-off recorded before anyone writes code.
Phase 2 of the plan is coded. Before I close it, audit the phase diff against its DoD: no less, no more, and tell me which findings block it.
Get a second opinion on PR #318 from another model family before merge; I want only findings that were checked against the source.
This change adds a retry helper and a new dependency. I think we already have one in utils and the stdlib covers the rest — audit it before it lands.
The plan file is complete and about to be accepted. Attack it once from fresh context and drop anything you cannot quote.
Do these new tests prove behaviour or just mock the function they test? And is the webhook input validated before it hits the SQL?
Fammi fare una review incrociata con codex su questa PR, e verifica ogni finding sul codice prima di riportarlo.
Testa l'app in produzione con l'account di prova e dimmi se il preventivo si genera.
